THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:6853  CRL.P No. 12867 of 2023  ORDER

This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. praying to enlarge the petitioner/accused on bail in Crime No.81/2023 of Nayakanahatti Police Station, registered for the offence punishable under Section 363, 376 of IPC, Section 4, 6 and 17 of the POCSO, Act, 2012 read with Section 34 of IPC.

2. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner, the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent/State and perused the material on record.
3.

The case of the prosecution is that on 02.05.2023 at about 05:00 p.m., when the minor victim was returning to her house after attending the call of nature, the petitioner / accused No.1 forcibly took her near a overhead tank situated by the side of Kanive Maramma temple and repeatedly committed penetrative sexual assault on her.

4. The learned counsel for petitioner has contended that there is an in-ordinate delay in lodging the NC: 2024:KHC:6853 complaint which has not been explained and the FSL report also does not support the prosecution case.

He contends that the petitioner is in judicial custody from 23.05.2023,
for nearly 9 months and therefore, seeks to enlarge the petitioner on bail by imposing any conditions.
5. The learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the prayer contending that the victim has categorically stated about the heinous act committed by the petitioner and the trial is in progress.
Therefore, he contends that if the petitioner is enlarged on bail, he may flee from justice and attempt to tamper the witnesses.
6. I have perused the statements of the victim recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C.
A perusal of the same at this stage shows that there is a prima-facie against the petitioner.
According to the prosecution, the date of birth of the victim is 10.12.2011.
The incident took place on 02.05.2023.
Hence, victim was a minor aged only about 13 years as on the date of commission of the offence.

As per the final opinion regarding the medical examination conducted on the victim, victim might Punith Kumar vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142502701/
2 have undergone sexual intercourse or an act similar to that.

sentences.text: 8. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that FSL report is silent about the presence of seminal stains on the clothes etc. is not a ground to grant bail to the petitioner.
9. In view of the statement of the victim there is a prima-facie case against the petitioner.

Further,
the trial is in progress and therefore, as rightly contended by the learned High Court Government Pleader, if the petitioner is enlarged on bail, he may try to influence the victim and flee from justice.
10. Petition is therefore, dismissed.
